item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-308ce3da55e2c5d7","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"SIPRI found that Egypt’s official military-spending figures averaged about US$3.8 billion annually over the preceding decade despite extensive arms acquisitions, identified gaps and shortcomings in government reporting, and concluded that resolving the problem required greater transparency in military budgeting.","question_ids":["2B.8","5B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Pre-2023 institutional finding; relevant as inherited military-budget transparency context for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns Egyptian government reporting and military expenditure during the Sisi-era period, but does not establish a specific 2023 decision by Sisi.","limitations":["The supplied page summarizes the paper rather than providing its full empirical analysis.","No 2023 expenditure figure or specific corrective action is supplied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-89ec1ecc18dbe1e0","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"A comparative doctoral study found that Saudi Arabia’s and the United Arab Emirates’ support for Egypt between 2011 and 2015 was explained primarily by regime-security motives, with geostrategy playing a subordinate role; the support included the post-2013 military leadership headed by Abdel Fattah el-Sisi.","question_ids":["2B.2","2B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"2011-2015 historical finding, outside the target year but relevant to inherited external-support and regime-security context.","ruler_attribution":"The study identifies support for the Sisi-led post-2013 authorities but analyzes Gulf actors’ motives rather than attributing their decisions directly to Sisi.","limitations":["The supplied abstract does not provide specific events, amounts, or 2023 developments.","The study’s conclusion concerns Gulf-state policy motives, not an evaluation of Sisi’s effectiveness or legality."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6c0b9ebc1ceb0420","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Brookings testimony stated that repression under Sisi exceeded that under Mubarak and Nasser in the number of Egyptians killed, wounded, and detained, and characterized the repression as more ambitious and totalizing, including mass killings described by Human Rights Watch as Egypt’s worst in modern history.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"2015 assessment; outside 2023 but relevant to the inherited state-repression context.","ruler_attribution":"The testimony directly attributes the described repression to President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s government.","limitations":["This is an author’s testimony summary, not a supplied underlying case dataset.","It does not provide 2023-specific incidents or outcome measures."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6c0b9ebc1ceb0420","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Brookings testimony argued that Sisi’s heavy-handed Sinai security approach had fueled the extremist insurgency there, questioning Egypt’s reliability as a counterterrorism partner.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.9","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"2015 assessment; relevant as historical evidence about the security strategy inherited into 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The assessment directly attributes the Sinai approach to Sisi.","limitations":["The supplied text reports an expert assessment rather than a causal study.","No 2023 insurgency outcome or policy correction is supplied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-507256de49844361","start_unit":14,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch and the Sinai Foundation for Human Rights reported that Egyptian authorities arbitrarily detained women and girls related to suspected ISIS-affiliate members in North Sinai, including some who had themselves suffered rape or forced marriage, and used detention to pressure male relatives or obtain information.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.7","3B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report was published in 2023 but documents cases from 2017-2022, providing direct near-period evidence.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the conduct to Egyptian authorities, including military, police, and National Security Agency personnel under Sisi’s government.","limitations":["The documented cases predate or only approach 2023; no 2023 case is specified.","The report relies on interviews and rights-group documentation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-507256de49844361","start_unit":15,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"The organizations documented 21 cases involving 19 women and two girls; relatives reported beatings and electric shocks, while 12 of the 21 were held incommunicado for periods ranging from two weeks to six months and six were forcibly disappeared.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Cases occurred between 2017 and 2022 and were reported in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The reported abuses were attributed to Egyptian National Security Agency, police, and military personnel.","limitations":["The cases are not 2023-specific.","Individual allegations were reported through relatives, lawyers, and formerly detained persons."]},{"source_id":"SRC-507256de49844361","start_unit":15,"end_unit":18,"fact_summary":"The report stated that security forces used “rotation” by filing new cases on the same terrorism-related charges to keep detainees imprisoned despite judicial release orders; it also reported that authorities failed to treat women and girls detained for ISIS-family ties as possible victims and did not provide rehabilitation or reintegration services.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","3B.7","3B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Documented practices and cases concern 2017-2022; reported in May 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The practices were attributed to Egyptian security forces and authorities.","limitations":["The supplied evidence does not establish Sisi’s personal order for any individual case.","The report presents rights-group findings rather than a court determination."]},{"source_id":"SRC-417ed09888d812e9","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"As a student at the U.S. Army War College during 2005-2006, Abdel Fattah el-Sisi wrote a 17-page thesis on possible paths to democracy in the Arab world.","question_ids":["8B.1"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"2005-2006, far outside the 2023 target period; possible background evidence of an articulated political program.","ruler_attribution":"The document directly identifies Sisi as the thesis author.","limitations":["The supplied material does not include the thesis text or its propositions.","It does not show that the ideas were adopted or implemented in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-668d1f08535729cc","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"A 2021 scholarly article reported that Sisi was carried by widespread public and media adulation after the 2013 events, with criticism described as minimal; it also described the emergence of Hasam alongside jihadist organizations, while noting that a direct Hasam-Muslim Brotherhood relationship had not been clearly demonstrated.","question_ids":["2B.2","3B.1","3B.2","3B.6","4B.1"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"2013-2019 historical analysis, outside the target year but relevant to inherited conflict and political-order context.","ruler_attribution":"The study attributes the coup’s leadership to Sisi and the repression to the Egyptian state-security apparatus.","limitations":["The supplied abstract does not provide 2023 developments or detailed incident evidence.","The relationship between Hasam and the Muslim Brotherhood is expressly unresolved."]},{"source_id":"SRC-047b1f21e8194c16","start_unit":1,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The World Bank Group’s FY2023-2027 Country Partnership Framework for Egypt set three high-level outcomes: more and better private-sector jobs, improved human-capital outcomes, and greater resilience to shocks;
